title: A hook write-set finding on a handler-authored hook is reported at `hooks[i].body.source` — a key the author never wrote — on both `os build` and `os lint`
body:
Filed unassigned from #16095 (branch `claude/issue-16095-hook-rules-reach-handler-authored-hooks`). Observed on `origin/main` @ `5d55afec4d` for `os build`, and on that branch for `os lint` once it judges the lowered view.

## What the author sees

Given

```ts
hooks: [{
  name: 'escalate',
  object: 'crm_case',
  events: ['afterUpdate'],
  handler: async (ctx) => {
    await ctx.api.object('crm_case').update({ id: ctx.input.id, is_escalated: true });
  },
}]
```

`os build` (and now `os lint`) reports `hook-api-update-readonly-field` with `where: hook "escalate" > body` and `path: hooks[0].body.source`. There is no `body` in the source file: the body exists only inside the lowered stack the command built. An author grepping their project for `body.source` finds nothing.

## Why it is shaped this way

`lowerCallables` replaces `handler: fn` with `handler: '<ref>'` plus `body: { language: 'js', source }`, and the validators (`validate-readonly-hook-writes.ts`, `validate-hook-body-writes.ts`) judge the stack they are given, so they cannot know the body was lowered. #16095 deliberately kept `os lint`'s output byte-identical to `os build`'s for the same hook (the repo's "same wording on every command" rule), so the remap belongs in one place, not in one command.

## Options

- A. Leave as is; document that a lowered hook's findings point at the lowered body (the `hook-bodies.mdx` write-set section now says lowering happens, but not where the path points).
- B. Have the registry runner (`runAuthoringRules`) or `lowerCallables` carry a `lowered-from` marker per hook, and have the two hook validators say `path: hooks[i].handler` plus a message suffix ("judged on the metadata body lowered from the inline handler") when it is set — one implementation, both commands agree.
- C. Emit both: keep `path` on the lowered body and add a `sourcePath` field pointing at `hooks[i].handler`.

B keeps the finding actionable without a second dialect; C is additive but widens the finding shape (a published contract for `--json` consumers).

Related: #16095 · #13653 (the readonly hook rule) · #4271 (the write-set rule's original scope).
